x_cursor_decision.choice: Keep observed_tail as a typed observation marker in Page/health/manifest/report metadata; remove it from the provider-pagination NextCursor and never use it as proof that the next UI read resumes after that item.
x_cursor_decision.why: XBrowser.Fetch never consumes q.Cursor. It searches a visible UI page and writes observed_tail from the last verified item. It is useful for provenance/dedup but not a provider continuation token. Current x_partial_test calls it a resume cursor and W07-02 asserts ADVANCED-PAST-READ-ITEMS; those claims exceed actual behavior.
invariants: Page.NextCursor is empty for visible X UI observations and Page.Complete remainsfalse. Full-body prefix, original per-item refs and observed span stay preserved.

ObservationMarker, e.g. observed_tail:<last verified upstream id>, is bound to source/query/requested window/exact observed items and persisted health or manifest. No marker is generated when no full item was read.
covered_until never advances from this marker; pending/uncovered window remains explicit in health/cycle. SourceCursor.opaque_cursor is not populated with new UI markers.

Subsequent X observations may reread visible posts; exact identity/hash dedup prevents new independent evidence inflation. Do not promise provider resume, mutate requested window, skip unseen intervals or infer ordering stability.

Recognize historical observed_tail:* values as legacy observation markers on read, preserve original receipts and data. Do not send them as real provider cursors, derive complete source-page chains from them, or perform destructive database cleanup. Any explicit canonical marker-normalization must be authorized by current capture/CAS and keep history.

Incomplete positive X without provider cursor still seals verifiable observed source bodies and health lineage; no fake source_pages completion or fabricated resume token is allowed merely to satisfy old test.
